ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is an AC power supply supplying power to the secondary side through a transformer, and the secondary-side voltage is marked as U2; the right side is a single-phase bridge fully controlled rectifier circuit composed of four controllable devices, with the output terminal connected to a resistive load R, and marked with DC output voltage Ud and current Id. Reasoning: Given R = 5Ω, U2 = 300V as the RMS value, and control angle α = 60°. When a single-phase bridge fully controlled rectifier circuit has a resistive load, the average output voltage is Ud = (sqrt(2) U2 / π)(1 + cos α). Substituting cos60° = 0.5 gives Ud = (sqrt(2) × 300 / π) × 1.5 ≈ 202.5V. Therefore Id = Ud / R = 202.5 / 5 ≈ 40.5A. The I2 / Id = 1.33 given in the problem does not need to be used for calculating Id.

method.method_draft: Read U2 = 300 V RMS, R = 5 ohm, and alpha = 60 degrees. Peak secondary voltage is U_m = sqrt(2)U2. For a resistive load, after firing at theta = alpha the current is i_d = U_m sin theta/R until theta = pi, then the next pair repeats the same pulse. Average over one rectified period: I_d = (1/pi) ∫_alpha^pi (U_m/R) sin theta dtheta = (sqrt(2)U2/(pi R))(1 + cos alpha). Substituting alpha = 60 degrees gives I_d = (sqrt(2)*300/(pi*5))*1.5 ≈ 40.5 A.
method.CoT_raw: Image description: The attached circuit diagram shows a transformer secondary labeled U2 feeding a single-phase fully controlled bridge rectifier made of four controlled devices, with a resistive load R on the DC output side and output quantities ud/id indicated. Reasoning: Read U2 = 300 V RMS, R = 5 ohm, and alpha = 60 degrees. The peak secondary voltage is Um = sqrt(2) U2. For a resistive load, after firing at theta = alpha, the load current is id = Um sin(theta) / R until theta = pi, and the next bridge pair repeats over the next rectified period. Therefore the average DC current is Id = (1/pi) * integral from alpha to pi of (Um/R) sin(theta) dtheta = (sqrt(2) U2 / (pi R)) * (1 + cos alpha). With alpha = 60 degrees, cos alpha = 0.5, so Id = (sqrt(2) * 300 / (pi * 5)) * 1.5 ≈ 40.5 A.
